newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close lower, seen finding feet.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close lower, seen finding feet.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed lower Tuesday on fears of a devaluation in Brazil but traders said the market may bottom out shortly.
"Today all we did was react to the Brazilian markets, tracking them lower. But we hope bonds here are about to switch back to gains after three days of losses," one dealer said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 shed 3/8 to 93-3/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.12 to 118.28.
Traders earlier in the day had linked the drop also to Finance Undersecretary Miguel Kiguel's statements late Monday saying a foreign debt buyback scheme was possible this year but not imminent.

"The market is going through some healthy profit-taking, which will allow it consolidate. Maybe it was better that it dropped more suddenly and didn't continue to drift aimlessly, although it doesn't help that we don't have a date for the buyback yet," another trader said.
